title: Nauta® Mixing Deep Dive — Title & Webinar Overview
description: Introductory presentation slide by Chris Paulsworth, Hosokawa Micron Powder Systems, establishing the scope of vertical conical screw mixing and drying technology.

title: Presenter Background & Hosokawa Pedigree
description: Background on Hosokawa Micron's historical ownership and ongoing engineering development of the genuine Vrieco-Nauta conical mixer brand.

title: Educational Webinar Objectives
description: Core goals: understanding convective conical mixing mechanisms, equipment anatomy, and engineering adaptations required for vacuum drying and freeze drying.

title: Table of Contents (Webinar Agenda)
description: Six-part roadmap: 1. Introduction, 2. Mixing Mechanics, 3. Component Breakdown, 4. Converting to Dryer, 5. Applications, 6. Q&A and Drawings.

title: Section 1: Introduction to Nauta® Mixers
description: Section opener establishing the conical vertical screw mixer as an industry standard for powder blending across pharmaceuticals, food, and advanced materials.

title: Conical Geometry & Gravity Discharge Benefits
description: Why conical geometry excels: steep vessel angle aids complete gravity discharge, minimizes residual heel, and eliminates horizontal bearing seals.

title: Section 2: How Nauta® Mixers Mix
description: Technical analysis of macro-convective transport, diffusive mixing, and velocity distribution inside an orbiting conical vessel.

title: Three-Action Conical Mixing Dynamics
description: Core triad kinematics: 1) Upward screw conveyance along the heated wall, 2) 360° orbital sweep dispersing material, 3) Gravitational core downward cascade.

title: Convective Circulation & Flow Patterns
description: Detailed cross-sectional flow vectors demonstrating continuous powder turnover without localized shear hot spots or mechanical compaction.

title: Low Shear Advantage for Fragile Powders
description: Preserving delicate crystal structures, frozen granules, and API particles: low Froude number mixing prevents attrition and unwanted particle breakdown.

title: 3D CFD Velocity Vectors across Conical Cross-Section
description: Computational fluid dynamics simulation showing velocity gradients between the high-velocity wall boundary and the central gravitational return zone.

title: Teamwork: Auger + Orbital Arm Dynamics
description: Key mechanical finding: the screw auger performs over 90% of the mechanical work, dictating a 10:1 motor power ratio relative to the orbital arm drive.

title: Motor Sizing, Torque Ratings & Start-up Loads
description: Engineering sizing rules for overcoming locked-bed starting torque, especially when dealing with damp, dense, or frozen granular cakes.

title: Filling the Mixer: 85% to 15% Batch Range
description: Operational flexibility: conical screw blenders operate effectively from 85% down to 15% working volume, accommodating variable batch sizing.

title: Section 3: Component Breakdown
description: Structural hardware teardown: agitator screws, universal joints, orbital arm drive assemblies, bottom seals, and discharge valves.

title: Mixing Screw (Auger) Flighting & Shaft Construction
description: Fabrication analysis of screw flighting: continuous helicoid versus sectional welded flights, shaft concentricity, and dynamic balancing.

title: Screw Metallurgy, Polishing & Surface Finishes
description: Hygienic 316L/Hastelloy specifications: electro-polishing down to Ra < 0.4 µm, crevice-free continuous seam welds, and sanitary cGMP passivations.

title: Orbital Arm, Universal Joint & Bevel Gearbox
description: Epicyclic drive kinematics: top drive gearbox rotating the central orbit arm while simultaneously imparting high-speed spin to the universal joint.

title: Bottom Bearing vs Cantilevered Design Comparison
description: Critical architectural decision: cantilevered screws eliminate bottom seal contamination in pharma AFD, while bottom pintle bearings support massive industrial screws.

title: Discharge Valve Technology (Ball Segment Valves)
description: Spherical segment valve seated perfectly flush with the bottom cone, eliminating dead-zones and preventing powder hold-up during freeze-dry sublimation.

title: Top Cover, Sanitary Nozzles & Motor Mounts
description: ASME VIII top dished dome layout: product charge nozzles, sight glasses, illumination ports, instrument thermowells, and drive head mounting flange.

title: Variable Speed Control & Drive Automation
description: Inverter/VFD modulation: slow agitation during initial freezing prevents cake cracking, while optimized speed during drying maximizes contact heat transfer.

title: Section 4: Using the Nauta Design for Vacuum Drying
description: The technological leap from blender to vacuum dryer: adding full vacuum containment, thermal jacketing, and vapor extraction infrastructure.

title: Mechanical Changes Required for Vacuum Duty
description: Full vacuum rating (-1.0 bar g), heavy vessel wall thickness, double mechanical shaft seals with sanitary nitrogen barriers, and heated vapor domes.

title: Heating Jacket Configurations: Half-Pipe vs Dimple
description: Comparing thermal jackets: external half-pipe coils provide superior structural rigidity and high thermal fluid velocity for rapid sublimation heat transfer.

title: Internally Heated Screw Augers (Rotary Unions)
description: Supplying thermal fluid directly through rotary joints into the screw flights, boosting effective heat transfer surface area by up to 40%.

title: Top-Mounted Vapor Filter Dome & Pulsejet Blowback
description: Heated filter housing located directly on the vessel head to prevent powder carryover into the condenser while eliminating cold-spot condensation.

title: Direct Comparison: Atmospheric Mixer vs Vacuum Dryer
description: Direct visual comparison of standard conical atmospheric mixer versus the jacketed vacuum dryer with filter column and workshop lifting rig.

title: Complete Turn-Key Vacuum Drying Process Skid
description: Complete process schematic: dryer vessel, vapor filter, primary condenser, condensate receiver tank, dry vacuum pump, and heating/cooling skid.

title: Solvent Condensation & Vacuum Pumping Train
description: Sublimation vapor path: vertical shell-and-tube surface condenser recovering solvent vapors ahead of a two-stage dry screw vacuum pump skid.

title: Heavy Powder Applications: Nuclear UO2 & Metal Powders
description: Case study on ultra-dense materials: uranium dioxide and iron powders with bulk density > 2.5 g/mL, highlighting high-torque drive reinforcement.

title: CAD Engineering Drawing: Top-Cover CIP Spray Nozzles
description: Authentic CAD cross-section (Scale 1:2) showing 5 sanitary CIP spray nozzles in the mixer cover, 115 mm pitch, providing 360° impingement over the orbital head.

title: CAD Engineering Drawing: Orbital Arm Positioner
description: Detailed engineering drawing of the top drive head with optional orbital arm positioner, central rotary union, and effective spray impingement envelope.
